content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text resolves a Matthew 1:16 dispute by asking what that individual verse's grammar admits rather than weighing the pressed chain against the defending chain by footing.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"never verse by verse: one reading allows the judge to decide the link by whether Matthew 1:16's own grammar admits both readings; the other requires the chain-versus-chain collision to be weighed by footing.","why":"The judge labels the point UNDERDETERMINED from the single verse's admitted ambiguity, which is the verse-by-verse treatment K-C forbids when the pressed witnesses are a chain."}
